title: Clarity Brief
learningObjective: Learn how to formulate unambiguous task prompts by separating task action, intended audience, explicit success criteria, and input source material.
whenToUse: Initiating unfamiliar or open-ended tasks where generic model responses would require repeated follow-up clarification.
Creating standard prompt templates for non-technical team members.
Setting strict criteria for summarization or synthesis.
whenNotToUse: Quick exploratory chats where conversational ambiguity is acceptable.
Highly complex multi-stage agent workflows that require iterative state tracking.
limitations: Does not eliminate hallucination risk on factual claims absent from the provided input.
Requires the prompt author to accurately define what success looks like.
template:
Task: [specific action]
Audience: [who will use the answer]
Success criteria: [what a good answer must contain]
Input:
[add the relevant material]

title: Expert Role
learningObjective: Learn how persona framing conditions the model's vocabulary and domain-specific heuristics to produce expert-level depth.
whenToUse: Technical reviews requiring domain jargon and specialized perspective.
Simulating specific stakeholder perspectives during product strategy or user interview preparation.
whenNotToUse: General-purpose factual lookups where role conditioning introduces unnecessary verbosity.
Using exaggerated or fictitious credentials to artificially induce model accuracy.
limitations: Role prompting changes stylistic tone and domain heuristics but does not grant the model factual knowledge it did not possess during training.
template:
Act as a [specific expert role]. Use the perspective and vocabulary of that role.
Task: [what you need done]

title: Structured Output
learningObjective: Learn how to constrain unstructured LLM text into predictable schemas (tables, JSON, itemized lists) suitable for downstream ingestion.
whenToUse: Generating data payloads intended for programmatic parsing or spreadsheet import.
Enforcing length limits to prevent runaway token costs and redundant verbosity.
whenNotToUse: Creative exploratory prose where strict structural rigidities dampen narrative nuance.
Complex nested database schemas that require formal JSON Schema schema-validation APIs.
limitations: Markdown tables and raw JSON strings in plain text output are not syntax-guaranteed unless validated by a deterministic schema validator.
template:
Return the answer as a [table / numbered list / JSON object].
Limit: [word or item limit].
Required fields or columns: [list them].

title: Context Block
learningObjective: Learn how to delimit authoritative reference text using XML tags to prevent the model from hallucinating external information or succumbing to prompt injection.
whenToUse: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) tasks where the answer must only cite provided documents.
Preventing untrusted user text from escaping its intended context boundaries.
whenNotToUse: Open-domain reasoning questions where external parametric knowledge is explicitly desired.
Very short prompts that do not reference any external document or text snippet.
limitations: The model may still occasionally summarize outside context if negative constraints are not firmly stated alongside the tags.
template:
Use only the context inside <context> tags.
<context>
[background, source material, constraints]
</context>
Task: [specific request]
